findings.title: NoMethodError when TopicUser record does not exist
findings.body: In the `unsubscribe` action, `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` on line 105 can return `nil` if the user has never interacted with the topic (no TopicUser row exists). Line 107 then calls `tu.notification_level` on nil, raising a NoMethodError and returning a 500 to the user. This is easily triggered by a user clicking the unsubscribe link in an email for a topic they were invited to but never visited.

findings.title: GET request performs state-changing unsubscribe operation
findings.body: The unsubscribe route is defined as a GET request (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`), but the controller action modifies the database (changes notification_level and saves). GET requests should be idempotent and safe. Email clients, link prefetchers, crawlers, and browser preview features may issue GET requests to this URL, inadvertently unsubscribing users. This should be a POST or PUT request with proper CSRF protection.

findings.title: Unescaped HTML rendering of topic title via triple-stache
findings.body: The template uses `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` (triple-stache, no escaping). The underlying locale string is `"You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}."` where `title` is `model.fancyTitle`. While `fancyTitle` on the server applies HTML escaping before SmartyPants, the client-side `fancyTitle` property may not guarantee the same escaping in all code paths. If any path provides an unescaped title, this becomes a stored XSS vector. The safe approach is to use a computed property that explicitly escapes the title and only allows the known `` tag, or use double-stache with a SafeString for the known markup.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link locale now requires unsubscribe_url but not all callers provide it
findings.body: The `unsubscribe_link` locale string was changed to include `%{unsubscribe_url}`. This string is rendered via `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` in `Email::MessageBuilder#body` and `#html_part` whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true. If any caller (current or future, including plugins) sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without providing `unsubscribe_url` in the options, I18n will raise `MissingInterpolationArgument`. The locale should handle the missing key gracefully, or the message builder should conditionally include the per-topic line only when `unsubscribe_url` is present.

findings.title: Unsubscribe action does not verify user can see the topic
findings.body: The `unsubscribe` action creates a `TopicView` and proceeds to modify the notification level without calling `guardian.ensure_can_see!(@topic_view.topic)`. While the practical impact is limited (the user only changes their own notification level), it leaks information: a user can confirm a topic ID exists and observe its title/slug in the rendered response even if they lack permission to view it.

findings.title: Typo in property name: stopNotificiationsText
findings.body: The computed property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (with 'Notificiations' misspelled — extra 'i' and missing 'o'). While this is consistently used in the template so it won't cause a runtime error, it makes the code harder to search for and maintain, and could cause confusion if other code tries to reference the correctly-spelled name.

findings.title: Test does not verify unsubscribe_url appears in the email body
findings.body: The test adds `unsubscribe_url` to the builder options but only asserts that `user_preferences_url` appears in the body and that the `List-Unsubscribe` header is present. There is no assertion that the per-topic unsubscribe URL actually appears in the rendered body or HTML part, which is the core feature being added. A test verifying that `unsubscribe_url` is interpolated into the body would catch regressions if the locale string or message builder changes.
